doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Being Charlie Shavers' bodyguard and rejecting racial divisions
summary: He guarded Charlie Shavers on a Southern tour with Dorsey and says the color line has no place in music.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: along in the business to avoid any of the pitfalls you might have run into, you should do it. You owe that to this business. Don’t get into racial scenes. I used to be Charlie Shaver’s bodyguard when we did a tour of the south. I mean I would go to the men’s room with him.

Dorsey. This was like late ’46, ’47, ’48 back in there. It was still hairy down in that area. But there’s really no room for that in our business. There’s no room for it anywhere really, but I mean you’re always going to have that problem, it’s just there, but especially in our business. I mean this is a talent business, and who you are and how you play, that’s it. There’s no room for the competing racial type things. There’s a couple going on now, you know very subtly, you know, White men can’t swing and all that. But we don’t need that. I mean the color line doesn’t exist as far as I’m concerned, anywhere, but especially in our business.
